transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Parallax Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Parallax Infra), Priya Nair (Parallax CTO)

Summary:
Parallax is evaluating migrating from OpenAI for most production inference to Redwood Dedicated for cost and latency predictability, with interest in compatibility with their existing vLLM/TGI-based stack and parity for evals. Key asks: model compatibility (hf checkpoints, TGI/vLLM), performance/latency numbers, security/compliance (SOC2, VPC, KMS), and a short pilot to validate cost + quality.

Topics:
- Current stack: OpenAI for prod, local vLLM for experiments, TGI for some models
- Compatibility concerns: tokenizer differences, generation hyperparams, KV cache behavior, function-calling parity
- Performance: latency SLOs, batching, quantization, throughput per GPU
- Security: VPC, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs, data residency
- Next steps: pricing worksheet, security docs, perf bench, pilot

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the deal. Ethan from our SE team is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya: Doing well, thanks. Appreciate you taking the time.
[00:10] Maya: Great. Quick agenda, want to understand current setup, constraints, what success looks like, then go into compat questions and pilot options. Ethan will chime in on technicals.
[00:20] Lena: Sounds good. To start, high level — we currently use OpenAI for most production text gen, embeddings to a lesser extent. We also run vLLM locally for experiments and use TGI in a few workflows. Main pain is cost variability and occasional latency spikes during big batches.
[00:36] Samir: and some of our legal folks are pushing for more control over data flows — need VPC or private deploy options.
[00:42] Ethan: Totally understood. Redwood Dedicated is aimed at that: reserved GPU pools, VPC peering, and private deployments if you need on-prem. We can also route overflow to Redwood Hosted if you want burst capacity.
[00:53] Lena: Two quick questions up front: 1) will our vLLM/TGI checkpoints run as-is on Dedicated? 2) will evals we ran against OpenAI match on Redwood?
[01:05] Ethan: short answer: mostly yes, but there are caveats. We support standard HF checkpoints and common conversion paths for TGI artifacts. vLLM is a runtime — if your models are standard transformer weights they should load. However tokenization, special generation knobs, and low-level kernel differences can cause slight output diffs. For eval parity we recommend running a side-by-side benchmark with your prompt set.
[01:30] Priya: can you elaborate on the "slight diffs" — we have hard thresholds on some metrics so even small differences matter.
[01:37] Ethan: Yeah, totally. Examples: different implementations of top-p sampling, subtle float precision changes after quantization, and KV-cache flushing semantics across runtimes can change early token choices. We provide config mappings for temperature/top_p/top_k, and we have quantization profiles that try to preserve quality. In practice 90-95% of prompts match closely, the tail cases need tuning or seed-preserving runs.
[01:58] Lena: okay. What about function calling / structured outputs? We rely heavily on a deterministic JSON schema for some flows.
[02:04] Ethan: We support function-calling APIs similar to Hosted — you can get structured outputs and we've added heuristics for more deterministic responses. If you have a strict schema, we suggest adding post-validators and a small eval suite during the pilot to measure regression.
[02:18] Samir: About performance — what's a realistic latency per token / per request compared to OpenAI? We need 200-300ms p95 on short chat messages, ideally.
[02:27] Ethan: Depends on model and sequence length. On Dedicated with A100 / H100 class nodes and the kernels we use, for a typical 2-4k context chat with small response it's possible to get p95 in the 120-350ms range with proper batching and caching. Batching helps throughput but can increase tail latency; we have autoscale and burst policies to keep p95 low. Also prefix/KV caching on recurrent user sessions reduces latency a lot.
[02:52] Priya: Are you using any special compilation or kernel selection? We currently use vLLM's kernel optimizations.
[02:58] Ethan: Yes, our runtime does model-specific kernel selection and some custom attention kernels; we also have quantization-friendly paths. In many cases we outperform stock vLLM on the same hardware because we optimize for production workloads with continuous batching and KV cache management. But benchmark results depend heavily on tokenization and request shape.
[03:18] Lena: cost is a big driver — can you give rough unit economics vs OpenAI?
[03:23] Maya: We'll send the detailed pricing worksheet, but ballpark — for high-volume predictable workloads Dedicated reduces unit cost by 30-60% vs purely hosted OpenAI rates depending on utilization, model family, and quantization. That's with reserved capacity.
[03:36] Samir: Do you support mixed mode — some routes on Hosted and others on Dedicated? For example, dev/test on Hosted, prod on Dedicated.
[03:44] Ethan: Yep. Smart routing by policy is a core feature — route by latency, cost, or region. You can pin models per route and have automatic fallback to Hosted if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
[03:56] Priya: Security — what about KMS, HSM, SSO, and audit logs? Our security team will require SOC2, SSO through SAML, and customer-managed keys.
[04:05] Maya: We support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit trails, and KMS integrations. For Private deployments we can integrate HSMs. We'll attach our SOC2 report and a security pack.
[04:14] Lena: Great. For the pilot, we want to run our evaluation set to check parity and measure cost/latency. How long does provisioning Dedicated take?
[04:21] Maya: For a pilot we can provision a small Dedicated pool in 3-7 business days depending on region and capacity. We also offer a 2-week pilot on a small dedicated instance to validate.
[04:31] Samir: During the pilot can we install our monitoring hooks? We have custom tracing and latency instrumentation.
[04:36] Ethan: Yes — Redwood Console exposes traces and per-token latency breakdowns; we can also route logs into your observability stack and add tracing hooks. We'll coordinate on the benchmark checklist so your instrumentation lines up with ours.
[04:47] Lena: About model conversion — we have a few TGI-specific args and a TGI-serialized model. Any gotchas there?
[04:54] Ethan: TGI artifacts are usually straightforward; we have a conversion path for TGI checkpoints but sometimes config keys differ. We'll need access to one example checkpoint during the POC to validate loadability and perf.
[05:06] Priya: Do you support multi-GPU sharding for large 70B+ models?
[05:10] Ethan: Yes, Dedicated supports tensor and pipeline parallelism, model sharding depending on the model. For very large models we provide guidance on memory/latency tradeoffs and quantization.
[05:21] Samir: On quantization — do you offer 4-bit or 8-bit profiles and what's the quality delta?
[05:26] Ethan: We have curated quantization profiles (8-bit and advanced 4-bit) with recommended fallback settings. Quality loss varies by model; our Optimize recommendations include eval signals to pick a profile that matches your quality threshold.
[05:38] Lena: Any customers done a migration from OpenAI to Dedicated recently with similar constraints?
[05:43] Maya: Yes, a fintech customer and a healthcare customer — both had strict compliance and moved to Dedicated. We can share anonymized benchmark slides and a case summary.
[05:52] Priya: On the eval parity testing — will you help run the side-by-side with OpenAI?
[05:56] Ethan: Absolutely. We'll help configure the runs, run the same prompt set against both backends, and produce a diff report (per-prompt metric deltas). We also have tooling to highlight prompts that diverge and the likely causes.
[06:10] Samir: For networking — how does VPC peering work and can we restrict egress?
[06:15] Maya: VPC peering and private link options are supported; for Private deployments you can have no public egress. We'll document the network topology options in the security pack.
[06:24] Lena: What's the SLA and uptime for Dedicated?
[06:27] Maya: SLA is provided on Reserved capacity contracts — typically financial uptime SLA plus latency targets for certain capacities. We'll include the SLA terms in the commercial pack.
[06:36] Priya: Ok — let's talk timeline. We're aiming to decide in the next 2-3 weeks and run a pilot in April if possible.
[06:43] Maya: That's reasonable. We'll aim to have pricing/sizing to you in 2 business days and security docs by Friday. If you approve the pilot we'll queue provisioning.
[06:52] Lena: Are there any limitations around model versions / forks? We do a lot of custom fine-tuning and sometimes have modified tokenizers.
[06:59] Ethan: Custom tokenizers are supported but may require a small integration step. We recommend sharing a sample tokenizer and a couple of tuned checkpoints so we can validate.
[07:09] Priya: What's the billing model for Dedicated pilot? Flat monthly pro-rated or trial credit?
[07:13] Maya: For pilots typically pro-rated reserved capacity with trial credits applied, we'll spell that out in the worksheet so you can model out cost.
[07:21] Samir: Any native support for on-prem air-gapped deployments? We have a long-term road for some regulated clients.
[07:26] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Private/offline packages are available. Those are longer engagements but we've done on-prem installs with HSM/KMS support.
[07:34] Lena: Good. A few nitty details: random seeds and determinism — sometimes we need deterministic outputs for certain pipelines. How do you handle seed control across different runtimes?
[07:43] Ethan: We expose seed control and deterministic sampling modes where possible; however quantization and certain kernels may still introduce nondeterminism. For strict determinism we recommend CPU deterministic runs or locked runtimes — we can discuss tradeoffs.
[07:56] Maya: quick note, we'll also share Redwood Console screenshots and a short diagram of how routing, caching, and fallbacks work.
[08:03] Lena: Lovely. If we run a side-by-side and see a 5% delta on a critical metric, what's the remediation path?
[08:10] Ethan: We'll triage — config mapping, quantization profile changes, prompting tweaks, or in extreme cases heavier compute to avoid quantization. We also have a rollback to Hosted option during rollouts.
[08:21] Samir: Are there known incompatibilities with vLLM features like search-based sampling or custom kernels?
[08:28] Ethan: Some vLLM custom kernels won't map 1:1; if you're using custom C++ kernels we may need to reimplement or adapt. Most users rely on standard HF weights and opt-level kernels.
[08:42] Priya: For the pilot we'll need an NDA addendum and list of support contacts.
[08:47] Maya: We'll attach the NDA addendum and list of contacts in the next email.
[08:51] Lena: Alright, let's record the concrete next steps.
[08:55] Maya: Action items quick recap: Maya to send pricing and sizing worksheet and security pack; Ethan to share benchmark checklist and perf templates; Parallax to send sample prompt set, tokenizer, and one checkpoint; Parallax to confirm compliance checklist.
[09:10] Priya: Sounds good. Also please include an onboarding timeline estimate for the pilot.
[09:15] Maya: Will do.
[09:18] Samir: One last question — do you have a list of recommended models / quantization settings for the types of tasks we run (summarization, customer chat, reranking)?
[09:26] Ethan: Yes, we'll include model & quantization recommendations with expected latency/cost tradeoffs per workload in the worksheet.
[09:33] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs by Friday. Any other questions?
[09:38] Lena: None from me. Thanks.
[09:40] Priya: Thanks all.
[09:42] Maya: Great, talk soon.

End of call.
